sections.prompt: What are the fund’s largest benchmark relative overweight and underweight Give rationale for both.
body_paragraphs: Sector Over/Underweights (Fund Level)
The Industrials sector is our largest sector overweight (+4.3%)
The Industrials overweight is linked to our SMID overweight.
Wasatch and Systematic SMID are particularly overweight Industrials
Small Cap indices have a higher Industrials weighting than Large Cap indices, so our Small Cap ETF holdings contribute to a fund level overweight
MFS and Systematic Large Cap are both overweight the fund’s index
Opportunistic Value has lower Industrials weights than the fund’s index
Financials is our second largest overweight (+2.5%)
MFS has a 7 percentage point overweight against its benchmark (Russell 1000 Value)
Our SMID overweight contributes somewhat to the fund-level overweight, as the Small Caps have a higher allocation to Financials than the fund’s index
Systematic Large Cap has a material overweight to Financials, with 18.3% of the strategy in that sector.
Despite the Financials overweight, the fund is slightly underweight banks (much of the overweight is due to financial services)
Two of our five single-stock overweights are Financials (Visa and BlackRock)
Information Technology is our largest sector underweight (-4.9%)
Clearbridge’s 42% allocation is higher than the fund’s benchmark weight, but is nearly 8% below the Russell 1000 Growth index’s weight
Systematic Large Cap is overweight IT
The Completion portfolio is all IT right now
Opportunistic Value is underweight the IT sector by over 10%
The SMID overweight contributes to a fund-level IT underweight as small cap indices have a much lower IT weight compared to large cap indices.
Sector Over/Underweights vs. STF (Opportunistic Value – Before Any Changes Made This Month)

Within Opp Value, our sector over/underweights are mostly consistent with prevailing spreads-to-fair. We are not increasing our real estate weight further as we are awaiting the rollout of the new REIT model.
Size/Style Relative Weights (Fund Level)
Our SMID overweight remains large (+7.5%)
This overweight is comprised of a 0.8% overweight to mid caps and a 6.7% overweight to small caps
We are also more value-leaning than our benchmark (see blue shaded area below):
Contribution to Tracking Error

The output from the most recent Axioma risk report is below. It shows that ~75% of our active risk is coming from “factor risk”—predominantly our IT underweight, momentum underweight, low beta, and small cap overweight. Specific active risk (stock specific risk) contributes the remaining 25% to our active risk. Fund-level ex ante risk is running at just over 3%. We are exploring ways of boosting this up and will present findings at the April PCC.
Largest Single Stock Over/Underweights (Fund)
Our largest single-stock overweights are the result of subadvisor stock selection as well as stock selection within Opp Value. No stock is more than 1% overweight at the fund level.
Mag 7/Elite 8 names comprise our top underweights at the fund level

sections.prompt: What moves are you making and what is your rationale?
body_paragraphs: Proposed trade:
Trim 0.5% each from S&P 600 Value ETF (SLYV) and S&P 600 ETF (SPSM)
Add 1% to Wasatch

This would simply formalize some of the cash changes we’ve made in the portfolio into actual target weight changes. The idea for this trade came out of our last quarterly call with Wasatch in January, when they showed that their portfolio was trading more cheaply than their small cap universe – a rarity since Wasatch focuses on higher quality companies.  The relative valuation opportunity has arisen because Wasatch’s portfolio has meaningfully underperformed our ETFs over trailing periods:
Trailing returns ended 2/28/2026

Wasatch’s performance history suggests they recover very strongly from down years, though there is no analogous year in recent memory for the disastrous stock selection that occurred in 2025. Wasatch is “down but not out”, and we believe it makes sense to push more into an active manager who has underperformed but who we continue to trust.

There are other portfolio considerations at play. This move may slightly improve the quality of our small cap exposure, and as we have noted small cap quality has underperformed small cap junk of late. MAR research suggests that small cap quality underperformance tends not to persist for more than two years and that “continuing underperformance would be an unprecedented event.”

Lastly, we would not be adding to small caps with this trade, just readjusting our exposure. If anything, we would be bringing slightly more balance to our style exposure within small caps by culling from small value/blend and reallocating towards small growth, a segment that has underperformed on a relative basis YTD.

sections.prompt: What macroeconomic environment do you believe your portfolio is best and worst positioned for?
body_paragraphs: Best Positioned For: We would expect the fund to outperform if IT struggles (e.g., wobbliness to the AI theme).
With overweights to Industrials, Financials and Small Caps, the fund is positioned for solid economic growth, if the growth is not purely driven by AI investment.
Worst Positioned For:  1.  Mag 7 and AI-themed market leadership.   2.  Small caps and value under-performing.

sections.prompt: What further comments would you like to make on current positioning and the proposed moves?
body_paragraphs: The selloff in software began around Halloween of 2025 (IGV’s most recent high-water mark). Since that time, our fund has performed in line with our benchmark but underperformed peers (see below). US Opp Value has performed well on a relative basis despite being overweight software in recent months. In other words, we have capacity to add more software within Opp Value by sourcing from areas that have performed well.
Prospective Opp Value trades

We are contemplating, but have yet to finalize, upcoming moves within Opp Value. As was discussed at the Equity PM meeting this month, we will be rationalizing our software holdings—eliminating some, adding to others—and exploring whether to add further to our software weight depending on how much of our portfolio is “software adjacent.” We are also considering trimming energy back to its target overweight as it has drifted further overweight given strong recent performance. Finally, we are looking to rationalize other parts of our book – e.g., potentially eliminating Campbell’s given its poor long-term performance and thesis drift.

sections.prompt: Roadmap---  What asset classes do you intend to do work on, or request that Research assign a squad to?  Briefly, why for each idea (VIR, cyclicality, unique catalyst, etc)?
body_paragraphs: We have met with all nine of our prospective managers in the US Large Growth bench refresh. We are individually scoring these prospects and will be meeting as a group to trim down the list and determine next steps.

On a separate but related note, Clearbridge intends to move to a non-diversified strategy from a diversified strategy, subject to the approval of its mutual fund shareholders. They do not anticipate that this move will lead to large immediate changes (~3% turnover).
In Opportunistic Value, we are reviewing the Information Technology sector this month.

sections.prompt: What are the fund’s largest benchmark relative overweight and underweight Give rationale for both.
body_paragraphs: Sector Over/Underweights (Fund Level)
The Industrials sector is our largest sector overweight (+3.8%)
The Industrials overweight is linked to our SMID overweight.
Wasatch and Systematic SMID are particularly overweight Industrials
Small Cap indices have a higher Industrials weighting than Large Cap indices, so our Small Cap ETF holdings contribute to a fund level overweight
MFS and Systematic Large Cap are both overweight the fund’s index
Opportunistic Value has lower Industrials weights than the fund’s index (~4% underweight)
Financials is our second largest overweight (+3.5%)
MFS is overweight financials compared to our fund’s benchmark, and 8 points over its style index.
Our SMID overweight contributes somewhat to the fund-level overweight, as the Small Caps have a higher allocation to Financials than the fund’s index
Systematic Large Cap has a material overweight to Financials, with 18% of the strategy in that sector.
Despite the Financials overweight, the fund is slightly underweight banks (much of the overweight is due to financial services)
The fund’s two largest single-stock overweights are Financials (Visa & BlackRock)
Information Technology is our largest sector underweight (-5%)
Clearbridge’s 45% allocation is higher than the fund’s benchmark weight, but below the Russell 1000 Growth index’s weight of 50%
Systematic Large Cap is overweight IT
The Completion portfolio is 80% IT (Apple and Microsoft)
Opportunistic Value is underweight the IT sector by ~8% as of the beginning of April; that has probably grown a bit through mid-May
The SMID overweight contributes to a fund-level IT underweight as small cap indices have a much lower IT weight compared to large cap indices.
Sector Over/Underweights vs. STF (Opportunistic Value – Before Any Changes Made This Month)
Within Opp Value, our sector over/underweights are generally consistent with prevailing spreads-to-fair as of April month end.
Size/Style Relative Weights (Fund Level)
Our SMID overweight remains large (+9.5%)
This overweight is comprised of a 2.4% overweight to mid caps and a 7.1% overweight to small caps
The increase in the SMID allocation was partially explained by Systematic LC Core’s decision to override soft guidelines regarding Small Caps and Mid Caps at the time of its March rebalance
We are also more value-leaning than our benchmark (see blue shaded area below):  The fund moved slightly toward Value compared with the previous month.
Contribution to Tracking Error

The output from the most recent Axioma risk report is below. It shows that ~75% of our active risk is coming from “factor risk”—predominantly our IT underweight, momentum underweight, low beta, and small cap overweight. Specific active risk (stock specific risk) contributes the remaining 25% to our active risk. Fund-level ex ante risk is running at 3.6%. We continue to  explore ways of boosting this in accordance with recent PCC presentations.
We note that the largest contributors to active risk are underweights to Alphabet, Apple, and three semiconductor companies.
Largest Single Stock Over/Underweights (Fund)
Our largest single-stock overweights are the result of subadvisor stock selection as well as stock selection within Opp Value. No stock is more than 1% overweight at the fund level.
Mag 7/Elite 8 names comprise our top underweights at the fund level.  Also prevalent among the largest underweights are Micron, AMD and Intel.

body_paragraphs: Fund Level Activities

After we line up IT sector replacements within Opportunistic Value, we plan to shift some or all of our Apple shares to the Completion portfolio.  Apple is our second largest underweight at the fund level.  If we shifted weight from Opp Value to the Completion Sleeve related to AAPL, we may add to Opp Value the proceeds of trims from the ETFs.

Semiconductor Positioning
